speaker: Doctor
text: Tell me, was there any specific moment during the accident when you heard a snap or felt a sudden shift in your leg? Also, is the pain in your right groin worse when you try to walk or stand?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To further characterize the injury, can you describe exactly how your right leg is currently positioned when you are lying down, and does it hurt significantly more to try to lift your foot off the ground?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray, Sacroiliac_Joint_X-Ray.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please return the AP Pelvis and Lateral Sacrum images.
This specific positioning—shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg—is highly suggestive of a posterior hip dislocation; please confirm if you can actively move your right hip or if the joint feels completely locked.
